# .github/: CI, deploy and the Targets workflow

Notes for anyone editing `workflows/ci.yml` or `workflows/targets.yml`, or reading their results. What every contributor must know (CI is the authority, generated files belong to CI) is in the root `AGENTS.md`.

- **Native CI toolchain:** Ubuntu 24.04 with gcc 13, clang 22 (apt.llvm.org) + `libclang-rt-22-dev`, gdb 15, valgrind 3.22, Node ≥22, FFmpeg. Stored targets: macOS arm64 and ubuntu-24.04-arm (all samples), windows-latest (`platform` samples). The `project-runner` job in `targets.yml` runs `check.mjs` (`make test` on the starter and solution zips of each project in its matrix, today Mario and Credit) on macos-14 and ubuntu-24.04-arm; on PRs it also runs when a path in the `pull_request` filter of `targets.yml` changes (`tools/check` except `*.md`, `tools/ci/verify-project-run.ts`, `src/testing`, those projects, `targets.yml` itself). Windows is not run (WSL only).
- **Reference environment.** Unless the change is docs-only (see the next note), the `check` job logs the runner image (`ImageOS`, `ImageVersion`) and the versions of gcc-13, clang-22, gdb, valgrind, node and ffmpeg; the `deploy` job installs nothing and logs nothing. We select the gcc major version by package name (`gcc-13`) and accept patch drift in clang 22 (apt.llvm.org) and the other apt tools. `verify --check` ignores version strings (`generatedBy`, each target's `compiler`) and compares behaviour only, so drift cannot turn it red.
- **CI-owned generated files.** On a same-repo PR that is not docs-only, the `check` job runs `npm run verify` with a read-only token. If `src/generated/{samples,traces}` changes in behaviour, it uploads the files, fails on purpose, and the separate `commit-generated` job (the only one with `contents: write` and `actions: write`; it runs none of the PR's build or test code, only `tools/ci/unpack-generated.mjs`, which accepts nothing but regular files strictly under `src/generated/{samples,traces}/`) commits them as `github-actions[bot]` to the PR branch and dispatches CI for the new head (a push made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` triggers no workflow, `workflow_dispatch` is exempt). The checks on the final head SHA come from the dispatched run. If the branch moved meanwhile, the bot skips the push and your own push gets its own run. Fork PRs cannot be pushed to and just fail `verify --check`. Timed-out runs are never cached (`cacheRuns` in `tools/verify/cache.ts`).
- **Docs-only pull requests.** The `changes` job runs `tools/ci/docs-only.mjs` on the merge commit's diff (`HEAD^1..HEAD`, `fetch-depth: 2`). If every changed file is the root `README.md` or `PLAN.md`, an `AGENTS.md` in any folder outside `content/modules/` (the app bundles Markdown from exercise and project folders), a skill's `SKILL.md` or `.claude/skills/` link, `LICENSE` or under `research/`, `check` skips the native toolchain install, version log, verify, trace, exercises, videos, animations, typecheck, `npm test`, build, e2e and the WebM transcode, and runs only `lint:content` and `vitest run tools/docs tools/ci` (the agent-notes and classifier tests that `npm test` would run). `check` still reports, so a required status never hangs (a trigger-level `paths-ignore` would leave it pending). Pushes, manual and bot-dispatched runs always run everything, so `deploy` is unchanged. It is an allowlist, not `**/*.md`: tooling reads Markdown under `content/` and `tools/`. `CLAUDE.md` is not on it because the repo forbids that file. Add a path only if no tool or test reads it.
- **`targets.yml` on PRs.** `gh pr checks`/`gh run list` show its runs under the workflow name `Targets`; only `project-runner` runs on a PR (the sample job is skipped). The `targets` concurrency group is per-ref for PRs so a PR run never queues behind `main`. Apple clang on `macos-14` is 15.0 and `make` is 3.81, so keep Makefiles 3.81-safe.
